items.claim: The row closes at Eccl.2.19 on the strength of the savoti turning-verb opening 2.20, but never discloses that the tachat-hashemesh refrain running through its own three verses continues unbroken past that same seam into 2.20 and 2.22.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.2.17 and oshb:Eccl.2.18 both carry תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ, and oshb:Eccl.2.19 closes on the same formula; the identical formula recurs immediately across the row's own boundary at oshb:Eccl.2.20 (תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ) and again at oshb:Eccl.2.22 (תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ) — a tier-1 frame-spine device present on both sides of the 2.19|2.20 seam. The row's device_notes address only the internal 2.17/2.18 sane'ti pairing and never weigh this continuing refrain as counter-evidence against the seam it draws, even though observed_substrate_signals already tags tachat_hashemesh for this row without disclosing its cross-seam continuation.

items.claim: The savoti turning-formula opening Eccl.2.20 is a genuine, byte-distinct verb from the shuv-root resumptive family tracked elsewhere in the book, correctly disclosed as a non-conflated rival, and the row's two 'gam zeh hevel' verdicts at 2.21 and 2.23 mark a coherent internal statement-plus-question-plus-verdict argument rather than an over-cluster.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.2.20 opens וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי (root savav), distinct from the shuv-root shavti forms sited elsewhere in the book (4.1, 4.7, 9.11) that the row correctly declines to conflate with it; the row closes on its own hevel-verdicts at 2.21 and 2.23, not on the neighboring row's material.

items.claim: The enjoyment conclusion at Eccl.2.24 and the closing hevel/reut-ruach double verdict at 2.26 correctly bound the quest narrative's own close, and the boundary into 3.1 correctly names a formal register shift (the fixed et-clause template) rather than resting on a tier-4 signal alone.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.2.26 closes with both the hevel and reut-ruach refrains firing together, and oshb:Eccl.3.1 opens the fixed et-plus-infinitive catalogue template immediately after; the eat-plus-drink pairing at 2.24 is correctly counted as one of the book's five such sites (sweep: 5 verses), matching the staged inventory.

items.claim: The time catalogue is correctly chunked as one list_catalogue row per the owner ruling, and its SAMEKH brackets at 3.1 and 3.8 are correctly disclosed as tier-3, single-witness corroboration, never conflated with the book's one PE.
items.evidence: The tier-3 parashah inventory records SAMEKH at Eccl.3.1 and Eccl.3.8 only, with no PE at either verse; the row's boundary_evidence_refs label both correctly as setumah, single-witness, tier-3; the 29-token et-count across the poem is disclosed as the staged inventory's own figure rather than claimed as an independently re-tallied digit.

items.claim: The mah-yitron echo linking Eccl.3.9 back to 1.3 is byte-true and correctly disclosed in boundary_evidence_refs, satisfying the cross-row mirror requirement, and the row's close at 3.11 before the yadati-marked restart at 3.12 is a genuine distinct-verb boundary.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.1.3 and oshb:Eccl.3.9 both open on מַה יִּתְרוֹן֙ (same root); oshb:Eccl.3.12 opens with the verb of knowing (yadati), a form absent from 3.9-11; the row correctly hedges the 1.3 citation as an echo rather than claiming 1.3 as part of this row's own span.

items.claim: The rejected alternative misdescribes the neighboring row (Eccl.3.9-11) as opening with 'the I saw burden-observation' when that row's own opening verse (3.9) is the mah-yitron question; the perception verb first appears mid-row at 3.10, so the rival's precision is weaker than claimed even though the yadati-verb boundary itself remains defensible.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.3.9 opens מַה יִּתְרוֹן֙ (a question, no perception-verb root); the perception verb רָאִ֣יתִי occurs first at oshb:Eccl.3.10, the neighboring row's second verse, not its opening one; the strongest_rejected_alternative nonetheless characterizes 'the row before it' as opening with that verb.

items.claim: The doubled self-address formula opening both Eccl.3.17 and 3.18 is byte-identical (verified by direct string comparison of the spliced tokens), a legitimate anaphoric pair justifying the row keeping the two verses together, and the row correctly flags forward -- without folding 3.19-21 into its own span -- that 3.18's animal language is developed by the following row.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.3.17 and oshb:Eccl.3.18 both open on the identical string אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י; the behemah token at the row's own close (3.18) recurs at oshb:Eccl.3.19 (three times) and 3.21, which the boundary_rationale discloses as content the next row develops rather than silently omitting it.

items.claim: The animal-comparison argument at Eccl.3.19-21 is correctly bounded as one continuous clause chain closing on the unanswered ruach-direction question, with the ra'iti-formula at 3.22 correctly marking a fresh, independently-verdicted unit rather than a fourth clause of this argument.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.3.22 opens with the ra'iti (I saw) formula, consistent with the same verb-marks-new-unit convention used earlier in this span (3.10, 3.16); no Elohim-family token occurs anywhere in 3.19-21 (byte-checked), correctly matching the row's own disclosure that it makes no divine-name claim within its own span.
